summary.headline: Capacite Q2 FY27 revenue hit a record INR771 crore (+19% YoY), but PAT fell to INR48 crore from INR51 crore on commodity-driven margin pressure.
summary.overview: Management reported record quarterly revenue of INR771 crore, up 19% YoY, with EBITDA of INR119 crore (15.5% margin) and PAT of INR48 crore (6.1% margin). H1 FY27 revenue was INR1,400 crore (+13%) while H1 PAT fell to INR87 crore from INR98 crore. Order book stood at INR13,013 crore as on September 30, 2026, with INR2,487 crore of orders secured in FY27 so far. Management said elevated steel, aluminium and electrical item prices weigh on margins, partly offset by escalation clauses, and that no fresh commodity provision was taken in Q2.

financial_highlights.change: vs INR51 crore in Q2 FY26
vs INR98 crore in H1 FY26

financial_highlights.value: INR13,013 crore as on Sep 30, 2026 (54% public, 46% private)

segments.name: CIDCO
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 certified sales of about INR177-178 crore, run rate close to INR30 crore per month; management expects 35-40% increase in Q3 and Q4, and at least INR50 crore per month next year.

segments.name: MHADA
segments.commentary: H1 FY27 revenue about INR123-124 crore; 25 of 34 rehab towers received, with a rehab work front of about INR4,200-4,300 crore (price variation included); company share about 35%.

segments.name: NBCC
segments.commentary: Run rate crossed INR60 crore per month; NGT disruption in November, with INR65-70 crore per month expected in non-NGT periods.

segments.name: Signature Global (Titanium Phase 1)
segments.commentary: Running at close to INR15 crore per month before NGT impact; expected to reach INR18-19 crore per month from Q4 FY27.

segments.name: IIT Bombay
segments.commentary: Only one location (INR70 crore of INR550 crore contract) handed over so far; full frontage expected by March 31, 2027, implying about INR60 crore per quarter over 24 months.

guidance_outlook: FY27 order inflow target of INR4,500 crore; company says it has secured about INR2,500 crore so far and expects to surpass the target, with INR3,270 crore under active negotiation.
FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 15.5-16.5% and cash PAT margin of 10.5-11.25% maintained; management will revisit in Q4 if commodity escalation catches up.
FY28 revenue guidance of INR4,000 crore reconfirmed; management expects fixed asset turnover above 5x at that level.
Mahindra Lifespace revenue expected to start from Q1 FY28, possibly Q4 FY27.
Standalone debt expected to fall or stay in line with March 31, 2026 net debt levels; about INR135 crore capex planned in FY27, with about INR10 crore monthly term loan repayment.
Recovery of INR52-54 crore from old debtors targeted in FY27; INR48 crore of assets held for sale targeted in H2.
capex_capacity: Formwork and plant purchases: INR64.2 crore formwork and INR10.57 crore plant and machinery in H1 (management first said INR127 crore total, then corrected).
Budgeted procurement of INR135-140 crore to be completed in FY27, with the balance in H2.
Core fixed asset turnover of 4.7x for the quarter ended September 30, 2026.
Aluminium formwork written off over 7 years; project execution period reduced from 4.5 years to 3 years, so depreciation is expected to stay at current levels or rise.
Q2 depreciation about INR35 crore (up from 29% of revenue per analyst question).
demand_pricing: Public sector 54% and private sector 46% of order book; management targets roughly 55:45 government-private mix over time.
Private sector contracts are 100% pass-through for commodities; government contracts rely on WPI and commodity-based price variation with about a 6-9 month lag.
Escalation gap for government projects narrowed from 5-6% in Q1 to about 2% in Q2 per management.

Steel prices rose to about INR62,000 per tonne from INR47,000 three months ago; aluminium formwork rose from INR10,500 to INR14,500 per sq m (40%), with expected correction to INR12,000-12,500 for future procurement.
NGT restrictions in Delhi NCR: complete ban from November 5 to 20, 2026 (about 15 days); company has factored INR45-50 crore of revenue loss for Q3.

qa_highlights.question: What makes up contract assets and receivables, and how much is retention versus unbilled?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said retention is INR170 crore; contract assets (WIP milestone billings) were about INR1,188 crore after a INR217.62 crore negative contract asset adjustment. Net receivables plus unbilled were about INR2,400 crore, or 77-78% of FY27 revenue; debtors are about 120 days. It disputed peer comparisons of 18-20%.

qa_highlights.question: Will commodity provisions reverse?
qa_highlights.answer: No provision was taken in Q2. Reversal depends on government escalation catching up with commodity prices; a decision is possible for Q4 after a Q3 review. Management declined to predict market moves.

qa_highlights.question: Will the company hit FY28 revenue target of INR4,000 crore and what is the capex and cash implication?
qa_highlights.answer: Guidance reconfirmed. Capex is driven by order intake; management expects positive cash flow after term loan repayment of INR101 crore last year and cash PAT margin of 10.5-11.5%.

qa_highlights.question: Why is bottom-line growth flat in H1 despite revenue growth?
qa_highlights.answer: Last year's PAT was helped by recoveries of bad debts and sale of non-core assets. Management expects INR48 crore of held-for-sale asset sales in H2 to lift margins if realised; operating EBITDA guidance is unchanged.

qa_highlights.question: How will NGT restrictions affect execution, and what NCR revenue share applies?
qa_highlights.answer: Management assumes a 15-20 day disruption can be absorbed; a 45-day disruption cannot be quantified. It did not disclose the NCR share of H1 revenue.

qa_highlights.question: What is the status of the promoter share pledge?
qa_highlights.answer: Pledge reduced; only 50 lakh shares remain pledged for the SBI project limit, which fell from INR608 crore to INR140 crore. Completion targeted by March 31, 2027, with no further pledges to NBFCs.

risks_watch: Contract assets and receivables are high at about 77-78% of FY27 revenue (about 120-day debtor days); the aging was promised by email and not disclosed on the call.
Escalation gap on government contracts and possible further commodity provisions; margin guidance depends on Q3 catch-up.
NGT disruption in Delhi NCR during November-December; a 45-day disruption would be unquantified.
Election-related labour availability in Q4 FY27 (UP elections); Q1 FY27 revenue dipped due to Bengal elections.
Execution timing risk on MHADA rehab towers, CIDCO new scope (expected in Q1 FY28) and IIT Bombay frontage handover by March 31, 2027.
Recovery of old receivables, with INR100 crore still pending against settlements; settlement agreements not yet finalised.
summary.management_tone: Confident on top-line growth, order inflow and FY28 targets, but cautious and non-committal on margin recovery, which management ties explicitly to commodity and escalation outcomes. Several answers were deflective (aging, NCR share, Maldives margin) and some figures were corrected mid-call (formwork purchases).
key_quotes: we have delivered another strong quarter, achieving our highest ever quarterly revenue of INR771 crores, representing a 19% Y-on-Y growth despite the seasonal challenges.
Our growth is backed by a strong and diversified order book of INR13,000 crores as on September 30, 2026, providing excellent revenue visibility for the coming years.
I don't see any reason why on INR4,000 crores, it will not be well above 5, again, an industry-leading number.
So the gap was 5% or 6% in quarter 1, the gap has come down to maybe 2% as I told last quarter also, it takes 6 to 9 months.

growth.why: FY28 revenue guidance of INR4,000 crore is reaffirmed, with a 13% H1 revenue rise and a CIDCO run-rate target of INR50 crore/month, backed by an order book of INR13,013 crore; no owned capacity additions are quantified and FY27 EBITDA margin guidance of 15.5-16.5% is held.
